newsitem.title: USA: Export Business - Grain/oilseeds complex - April 24.
newsitem.headline: Export Business - Grain/oilseeds complex - April 24.

text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Algeria recently bought several cargoes of durum wheat, probably Canadian, at prices ranging from $210 to $215 per tonne, cost and freight, European grain exporters said. Algeria was initially seeking 100,000 tonnes of optional durum wheat for shipment in May and June. But exporters said it may have purchased less than 100,000 tonnes.
- Japan's Food Agency said it bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 20,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat and 40,000 tonnes of Australian wheat at its weekly tender, all for June shipment.
CORN SALE - An Indonesian feed mill has bought some 50,000 tonnes of corn from Argentina for around US$142-$144 a tonne C&F for July shipment, dealers said on Thursday.

SOYMEAL SALE - Hong Kong grain traders confirmed on Thursday that China bought 100,000 tonnes of South American soymeal for delivery at the end of May or beginning of June to a south China port but were not sure of the price.
WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd has invited tenders to buy 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday, a company official said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Jordan was to tender May 1 for 120,000 tonnes of U.S. HRW and/or northern spring wheat for May/June.
BARLEY TENDER - Turkey on April 29 seeks 150,000 tonnes of barley in three 50,000-tonne shipments. It seeks white feed and malting white barley for May 15-22, June 1-15 and June 1-15 shipment.
RICE TENDER - South Korea is to tender at the end of June to buy 77,000 tonnes of rice to meet its 1997 WTO quota.
SOYBEAN TENDER - CCC was tendering on April 30 for up to 10,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow soybeans for export to Ukraine, May 10-June 5 shipment.
SOYMEAL TENDER - El Salvador is to tender April 28 for 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of PL-480 soybean meal for May 7-22 shipment, the buyer's agent said.

COMMODITY TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp of USDA said it will tender April 29 for pinto beans, sunflower oil, bulgur and wheat-soy blend for donation to Moldova. It seeks 255 tonnes of pinto beans, 605 tonnes of sunflower oil, 510 tonnes of bulgur (cracked wheat), and 255 tonnes of a wheat-soy blend. The beans, bulgur and wheat-soy blend were for June 6-20 shipment and the oil was for June 20-July 5.

MARKET TALK - The European Union, anxious to protect domestic supplies in the face of mounting drought fears and volatile prices, on Thursday slapped taxes on its daily exports of soft wheat grain and flour. The move brings this season's EU wheat exports to a halt.
The EU also approved on Thursday a 200,000 tonne quota for the import of high quality soft wheat and durum wheat into the Community, the French national cereals office ONIC said.
The total was made up of 100,000 tonnes of soft wheat and 100,000 tonnes of durum wheat. Several U.S. exporters said they were somewhat surprised about the quota but not the tax.
"That would be somewhat unusual," one U.S. exporter said, referring to the import of 100,000 tonnes of soft wheat.
"We knew that they were done for old crop exports for their crop year," the exporter added. "Come new crop, we have plenty of soft white wheat to sell."
He noted the EU move reconfirms that the key suppliers of world wheat would be the United States, Canada and to a lesser extent Australia for the summer months of June, July, August and September.
"So that perceived demand for the summer should come to the U.S. or Canada," he said.
Another exporter said the EU move was a positive for U.S. wheat exports. "It will change the world balance sheet, that's for sure," he said.
Pakistan, facing flour shortages, may seek more wheat this weekend than many U.S. exporters had initially speculated, exporters said.

Several U.S. exporters had said on Wednesday that Pakistan might tender for anywhere from 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of optional origin soft white wheat as early as this weekend, with the United States the most likely supplier.
Quantities now ranged from seven cargoes, totaling about 315,000 tonnes to up to 600,000 tonnes, one exporter said.

.. Indonesian buyers are seeking between 20,000-50,000 tonnes of corn and over 50,000 tonnes of soymeal after recently buying a Panamax-sized cargo of Argentine corn for July shipment, dealers said on Thursday.
